data.why: The app loads data/spectra.csv (70 dyes, FPbase-derived excitation/emission spectra) automatically at startup via load_builtin(); no upload is needed to use either tab.

goals: Build a spectral flow panel: for each marker, list the dyes on hand and let the app pick one dye per marker that keeps the most similar pair as different as possible
Protect key markers by ticking them so their dyes are kept furthest from every other dye in the panel
Check a proposed/existing panel's similarity matrix and worst-pair table to see which dye pairs will be hard to unmix
Read the complexity index (condition number) of a candidate panel as a single easier-to-unmix-or-not score
Download the ranked table of candidate panels as a CSV for the experiment record
Optionally substitute measured single-stain reference signatures (a CSV upload) in place of the simulated FPbase signatures if real control data is available

review.summary: This is a faithful, well-staged tree for a spectral-panel picker. Its goal and phases match the README's two modes (pick by maximin similarity with key markers; check an existing panel), and the independent replay reproduced every task and feature. It needs small fixes before filing: the 'rows' colouring wording, two screen citations that don't show the cited download, the unmodelled no-dye-twice and search-stopped branches, and a feature for the reference-signature swap.
